I am writing about a problem that our entire street has been facing since the beginning of last month and which I have already raised twice by telephone with the ward office without any result whatsoever. Our street is a narrow residential lane with about thirty houses on it and a small provision store at the far end. Some time in the first week of last month a contracting crew arrived, without any prior notice to the residents, and began digging a trench along the left side of the road, apparently in connection with laying an underground cable of some kind. They worked for three days, dug a channel roughly two feet wide and about three feet deep along almost the entire length of the lane, laid what looked like a black conduit pipe in part of it, and then simply stopped coming. Nobody has returned since. The trench is still open along most of its length. In two places they have put a wooden plank across it so that people can walk over, and in one place there is a piece of blue plastic sheet weighted with stones, but there are no barricades of any kind, no warning tape, and certainly no lights at night. The soil that was dug out is heaped along the edge and with the rain it has begun washing back into the channel, so the depth is no longer even consistent. Two weeks ago an elderly gentleman from house number 21 stepped into it after dark and injured his knee badly enough that he is still using a walking stick. Children going to the school at the end of the road use this lane every morning and they walk past it within a foot. Autos can no longer enter the lane at all, which means that anyone needing to be taken to hospital has to be walked out to the main road first. I would like to know who authorised this work, why it was abandoned, and when the trench will be filled and the road restored.
adjudication: the taxonomy assigns abandoned excavation to CONSTRUCTION even when the hole is in the road surface; ROADS covers wear of an intact surface; abandoned excavation with an injury already recorded and access blocked for emergency vehicles

description: Respected sir madam, this is regarding the open drain that runs behind the houses on our cross which has been in a terrible state for as long as I have lived here which is now nine years. The drain is about three feet wide and it was originally built with concrete slabs over the top but most of those slabs are now either broken or missing entirely, I would say there are seven or eight gaps along the stretch behind our compound alone. Because the slabs are gone, all the household rubbish from the upper lane ends up inside the drain, and the flow stops completely. What happens then is that the water backs up and stands there for weeks at a stretch, completely black, with a very heavy smell that gets into the houses whenever the wind turns. There are mosquitoes in enormous numbers, and I am told by the doctor at the clinic that four or five dengue cases he has seen this season are all from these three lanes. When it rains properly the drain overflows and that black water comes up to the back doors of the ground floor houses including ours. We have complained about this at least four times over the years and each time somebody comes, looks at it, and leaves.
